Statement 1 therefore overreaches by writing 'cognizable/non-cognizable'. Section 173(3) is new to the BNSS and permits the officer in charge, for offences punishable with three years or more but less than seven years, to conduct a preliminary enquiry within fourteen days with the prior permission of an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police, which is what statement 2 describes. Section 173(1) says information 'may be given orally or by electronic communication', so electronic filing is an option, not an obligation, and statement 3 is wrong. Note there is no '1 and 2' option, so the paper itself treats exactly one of statements 1 and 2 as correct. RUNNER-UP: C ('1 only'). C wins if the examiner treats the '/non-cognizable' insertion as loose phrasing rather than an error, and instead reads statement 2 as wrong on the ground that a Zero-FIR station has no territorial jurisdiction and must transfer the FIR rather than enquire into it. That second reading is defensible; the reason I set it aside is that Section 173(3) attaches the enquiry power to the officer in charge who receives the information, without carving out zero-FIR receipts.
